gameMod.name: Recon-NG
gameMod.note: By Darkvalnar (https://github.com/Darkvalnar/hackhub-reconng) — an exploitation workspace: the player picks an exploit module, breaches a target, and works inside a persistent session. Quests that use this pack need it installed on the player's machine; list recon-ng under the mod's dependencies too (see the mod's own troubleshooting checklist).

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.SessionOpened
events.label: Breach: Session opened
events.docs: Fires when the player's exploit lands and a session opens — a foothold is enough for this one. Match the machine by host or IP, or the attack by module.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.DesktopOpened
events.label: Breach: Desktop opened
events.docs: Fires when a session goes desktop-grade through a GUI implant. Match on host or IP; the profile and system say which desktop the player sees.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.DirListed
events.label: Breach: Directory listed
events.docs: Fires when the player lists a directory inside a session. (Not on the mod's docs page — confirmed in its source.) Match on host and path.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.FileRead
events.label: Breach: File read
events.docs: Fires when the player reads a file with cat inside a session. Match the file by path or name, the machine by host or IP.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.FileDownloaded
events.label: Breach: File downloaded
events.docs: Fires when the player saves a session file to their downloads — the classic bring-me-proof objective. Match the file by path or name.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.FileDeleted
events.label: Breach: File deleted
events.docs: Fires when the player removes a file with rm. Only files you planted as deletable can go — match by path or name.

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.Shutdown
events.label: Breach: Machine shut down
events.docs: Fires when the player runs shutdown, poweroff or halt inside a session — the machine goes dark and the session ends. (Not on the mod's docs page — confirmed in its source.)

events.name: ReconNg.Breach.SessionClosed
events.label: Breach: Session closed
events.docs: Fires whenever a session ends for any reason — the player closed it, the story cut it, or the machine went dark. The reason says why: a story kick reports terminated.

events.name: ReconNg.UserEnum.Complete
events.label: User enum: Probe complete
events.docs: Fires when a username probe finishes against a host you registered for probing. (Not on the mod's docs page — confirmed in its source.) Match on host; the users list carries what came back.

storage.label: Plant evidence on a host
storage.docs: Adds a file to the host's breach session: when the player breaches the target, the file is there to read or download. Wire this at quest start, before the player can breach.

fields.label: Host or IP
fields.hint: The machine the file waits on. A domain name works.

fields.label: File path
fields.hint: Where the file sits in the session, like /opt/case/evidence.txt.

fields.label: File contents
fields.hint: What the file says — this is where your clue goes.

fields.label: The player can delete it
fields.hint: On lets the player remove the file with rm — drive an objective off the FileDeleted event. Off (the usual) keeps it.

storage.label: Offer a new exploit module
storage.docs: Teaches the player's recon-ng a brand-new exploit: the service, port, version and vulnerability it needs, and what privilege it grants. One version string and one vulnerability type per module here — most built-ins need only that. Wire it at quest start.

fields.label: Module id
fields.hint: Unique name like exploit/http/my_rce. Reusing an id replaces that module.

fields.label: Display name
fields.hint: What the player sees in the module list.

fields.label: Kind
fields.hint: Exploits breach; post modules run inside a session.

fields.label: Service
fields.hint: The canonical service on the matched port. https and web count as http; mysql, mariadb and postgres count as database.

fields.label: Port
fields.hint: The port the service listens on, like 80.

fields.label: Version it matches
fields.hint: The port's version must contain this text, like nginx 1.18.0.

fields.label: Vulnerability it needs
fields.hint: The target's domain must carry this type.

fields.label: Privilege it grants
fields.hint: How powerful the session is after the breach lands.

fields.label: Description
fields.hint: One line the player reads about this exploit.

storage.label: Let username probes work on a host
storage.docs: Registers a host for SSH username probing: the player's user_enum module recovers the account name here. The host also needs an active SSH port with an OpenSSH, Dropbear or libssh version. Wire it at quest start.

fields.label: Host or IP
fields.hint: The machine that answers probes. A domain name works.

fields.label: Account name it gives up
fields.hint: The one username the probe recovers, like svc.backup.

nodes.label: Cut the player's breach session
nodes.blurb: Kicks the player out of the host
nodes.docs: Ends the player's session on this host when the story reaches the node — a trace kicking in, an admin stepping in, a scripted beat. A blank message cuts silently (pair it with your own notification); anything you write is what the player reads. The SessionClosed event fires with reason terminated, so drive the follow-up off that.

fields.label: Host or IP
fields.hint: The machine whose session ends. A domain name works.

fields.label: What the player reads
fields.hint: Blank cuts silently; written text is shown, like Connection traced. Session terminated.

nodes.label: Open or close a host
nodes.blurb: Closes a host off — or opens it again
nodes.docs: Closes a host off entirely when the story reaches the node: while closed, the player cannot recon, check or breach it at all — as if it were not there. Flip it back on to bring a host online mid-story. Use this for a host that should not exist yet; a host the player found and is kept out of is a lock instead (the editor cannot write those yet).

fields.label: Host or IP
fields.hint: The machine to close or open. A domain name works.

fields.label: Host is open
fields.hint: Off closes the host off; on opens a host you closed before.
